title: Metabolic biotinylation of mammalian cell receptors for imaging
protocol: Clone BAP into pDisplay.
Insert the BAP sequence between the N-terminal epitope of hemagglutinin A (HA).
Precede the insertion with a signal sequence from the murine Ig kappa-chain V-J2-C.
Generate the pBAP-TM plasmid encoding the HA-BAP-TM protein (BAP-TM reporter).
Mix 5 µl Pfu buffer with each reaction.
Add 2.5 µl upstream primer to each reaction.
Add 2.5 µl downstream primer to each reaction.
Add 1.5 µl dNTPs mix to each reaction.
Add 1 µl pXa-1 plasmid to each reaction.
Add 5 µl DMSO to each reaction.
Add 1 µl Pfu DNA polymerase to each reaction.
Increase the volume of each reaction to 50 µl with autoclaved ddH2O.
Incubate at 95°C for 3 min.
Denature at 95°C for 30 sec for 35 cycles.
Anneal at 48°C for 30 sec for 35 cycles.
Extend at 72°C for 1 min for 35 cycles.
Extend at 72°C for 10 min after the final cycle.
Boil in a microwave 1g of agarose in 100 µl 1xTAE buffer until dissolved.
Add 5 µl ethidium bromide to the agarose solution.
Pour the gel into an electrophoresis apparatus and wait for solidification.
Load 50 µl PCR product with added 10 µl of 6x gel loading buffer into a well on the agarose gel.
Load 1kb DNA ladder (500 ng containing 1x GLB) in another lane on the agarose gel.
Run the gel at 80V for about 1hr at room temperature.
Check the size of the PCR product using UV light.
Excise the portion of gel containing the desired band using a razor blade.
Extract the DNA from the excised gel piece with Qiagen gel extraction kit as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Digest the purified PCR product with BglII and SacII in a 100 µl reaction by adding 10 µl 10x NEB buffer, 20 units of each restriction enzyme, and make up the rest of the volume with ddH₂O.
Simultaneously digest 5 µg pDisplay DNA under the same conditions as above.
Incubate all digestion reactions for 2-3 hours at 37°C.
Electrophorese the digested pDisplay DNA on a 1% agarose gel alongside a 1 kb DNA ladder.
Extract the single band corresponding to the digested pDisplay using Qiagen kit.
Purify the digested PCR product using the Qiagen kit without running it on the gel.
Quantify the amount of DNA by loading 2 µl of the digested backbone and PCR product along with a known amount of the 1 kb DNA marker on a 1% agarose gel.
Resolve the samples by electrophoresis to compare band intensity of the PCR product and vector to the DNA standard.
Estimate the concentration of DNA by eye.
Add 2 μl of 10x ligase buffer to a 20 μl reaction.
Add 30 fmoles of digested pDisplay DNA to the reaction.
Add 90 fmoles of PCR product to the reaction.
Add 1 μl of T4 DNA ligase at 400 units/μl to the reaction.
Make up the remaining volume with ddH2O.
Incubate the ligation reaction overnight at 14°C.
Transform 1 μl of the ligation into DH10B electrocompetent bacterial cells by adding it to 30 μl of cells.
Electroporate the mixture.
Increase the volume to 500 μl with SOC medium and incubate for 1 hour at 37°C with shaking.
Plate 200 μl onto an LB agar plate containing ampicillin.
Incubate the plate overnight at 37°C.
Pick 10 colonies from the plate.
Culture each colony in 4 mL of LB containing ampicillin (50 mg/L) overnight at 37°C with shaking.
Purify plasmid DNA from these cultures using a Qiagen miniprep kit.
Digest 5 μl of each purified DNA sample with Bgl II and Sac II restriction enzymes in a 20 μl reaction.
Electrophorese the digested DNA on a 1% agarose gel along with a 1kb DNA ladder.
Check for clones giving two bands corresponding to the digested plasmid (5.3 Kb) and PCR product (around 400 bp).
Transform the correct clone back into electrocompetent bacteria by electroporation.
Pick a single colony from the transformed cells.
Culture the picked colony as described previously.
Make glycerol stock by adding 100 μl of sterilized glycerol to 900 μl of bacterial culture containing the cloned DNA.
Quick freeze with dry ice/methanol bath.
Store at -80°C.
Expand clone in 200 mL of LB with ampicillin.
Purify plasmid DNA using Qiagen maxiprep kit.
Grow BHK-12 baby hamster kidney cells in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 100 U penicillin and 0.1 mg streptomycin per ml at 37°C and 5% CO2 in a humidified atmosphere.
Plate cells in p60 plates to achieve 70-80% confluency the next morning.
Add 10 µl lipofectamine to 200 µl OPTIMEM in tube 1.
Add 3 µg pBAP-TM DNA to 200 µl OPTIMEM in tube 2.
Mix tubes 1 and 2.
Incubate mixed solution for 45 min at room temperature.
Increase the volume of the mix to 1.5 mL with OPTIMEM.
Wash plates with OPTIMEM.
Add the lipofectamine-DNA mix to the plate wells.
Incubate at 37°C for 4 hrs with occasional rocking of the plates.
Remove the mix after 4 hours.
Add 3 mL of fresh growth media and return to 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Rinse cell monolayer once with PBS forty-eight hours post-transfection.
Harvest cells by scraping into 1.5 mL PBS.
Spin down the cells at 300g for 5 min.
Lysate cells by adding 50 µl lysis buffer supplemented with 0.5 µl protease inhibitor and incubating on ice for 30 min.
Centrifuge the lysed cell mixture at 10,000g for 30 min at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Quantify the total protein concentration of the cell lysate using the Bradford reagent assay.
Resolve 20-50 µg protein in lysate by SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) in running buffer with molecular weight standards.
Transfer proteins onto nitrocellulose membranes by electrolytic transfer in transfer buffer.
Stain membranes with Ponceau by adding it to the membrane and mixing for 1 min to verify even protein loading.
Block the membrane with 10% fat-free skim milk in TBST buffer for 1 hr at room temperature.
Incubate the membrane with 1 µg/ml streptavidin-horseradish peroxidase conjugate diluted in 5% fat-free skim milk in TBST for 30 min at room temperature with shaking.
Wash the membrane 3 times (15 min each) with TBST.
Add ECL reagent and shake for 1 min.
Insert membrane in a cassette, place film on top in the dark, and develop by autoradiography.
Incubate membrane with 0.2 µg/ml anti-HA antibody diluted in 2% fat-free skim milk in TBST for 1 hr at room temperature.
Place microscope cover glass in 12 well plate.
Coat the cover glass with 0.1 µg/mL poly-lysine in PBS for 1hr at 37°C.
Wash the coverglass with PBS.
Store the coated coverglass at 37°C until use.
Transfect cells as directed.
Replate transfected cells on poly-lysine-coated glass coverslips after 24 hours.
Transfer the coverslips into a clean 12 well plate for surface staining.
Wash cells once with DMEM.
Incubate cells with 0.4 μg/ml anti-HA antibody or anti-biotin antibody diluted in DMEM for 6 min at room temperature.
Wash cells quickly three times with DMEM.
Incubate cells with 20 µg/ml secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa594 for 30 min at room temperature in the dark, protected from light.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 10 min.
Wash cells again with PBS.
Mount coverslips on microscope slide using fluorescent mounting medium.
Analyze cells by confocal fluorescence microscopy.
Fix cells with 1.5% PFA for 10 min.
Wash cells three times with PBS.
Block coverslips with either 10% normal goat serum (NGS) and 1% BSA for HA detection or with SuperBlock blocking buffer for biotin detection, incubating for 1 hour at 37°C.
Incubate non-permeabilized cells with either 1 µg/mL anti-HA antibody diluted in 1% NGS or 10 µg/mL anti-biotin antibody diluted in 2% Superblock buffer at 37°C for 1 hr.
Wash coverslips three times with PBS.
Incubate coverslips with 2 µg/mL secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa594.
Collect transfected cells expressing BAP-TM or control cells by treating them with trypsin.
Pellet the collected cells by spinning down at 300g for 5 min (4°C) using a microcentrifuge.
Wash the pelleted cells once with PBS.
Incubate the cells with 10 µg/mL streptavidin-Alexa680 diluted in PBS containing 0.5% dialyzed BSA at 4°C for 20 min.
Wash the cells free of non-specific binding by removing excess reagent and resuspending them in fresh buffer.
Alternatively, incubate the cells with 20 µg/mL anti-biotin antibody diluted in PBS containing 0.5% BSA at room temperature for 6 min.
Wash the cells to remove any unbound antibody.
Incubate the cells with a secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa660 at room temperature for 30 min.
Resuspend the cells in 200 µl of PBS and analyze them using FACS.
Rinse the cells with PBS and resuspend them in culture media (about 5 million cells in 200 μl) in an eppendorf tube.
Add the viral vector so you have a multiplicity of infection (transducing units per cell) of 20 and incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Increase the volume with culture media and re-plate the cells.
Check eGFP expression after 48 hrs.
If the infection results are not satisfactory, repeat the infection one more time on the same cells.
Resuspend 5 million cells in 100 μL PBS.
Implant the cells subcutaneously in the back flanks of nude mice (6 weeks old, weighing 25-27 g), which have been anesthetized by intraperitoneal injection.
Inject mice with a mixture of ketamine (25 mg/L) and xylazine (5 mg/L).
Implant BAP-TM-expressing cells on one side of the mouse.
Implant control cells on the other side of the mouse.
Wait until tumors reach a size of 3-5 mm in diameter, approximately two weeks after implantation.
Inject mice intravenously with 70 nmoles/kg body weight of streptavidin-Alexa680 conjugate.
Image the mice 24 hours later by FMT under general isoflurane anesthesia (1-1.5% at 2 L/min).
Alternatively, inject mice with 70 nmoles/kg body weight of streptavidin.
Wait 18 hours to allow streptavidin to bind to biotin on the surface of tumor cells and for unbound streptavidin to be cleared from circulation.
Inject mice with a similar amount of biotinylated-MNP.
Image the mice with T2-weighted MR 24 hours later.
